description: Answers "Give me a quick due-diligence read on NVDA", "Is anything wrong at this company?" or "Brief me on Apple before the market opens". Give a ticker, company name, CIK or website domain. One call returns: who the company is (industry, HQ, CEO, founded, employees, description), four fiscal years of revenue, operating and net income, EPS, operating and free cash flow, cash, debt and equity with margins and growth (SEC XBRL), the latest quarter with year-over-year growth, the last 5 8-K events with item titles and excerpts, insider open-market buying and selling from the latest Form 4s (10b5-1 and tax sales set apart), the latest 10-K/10-Q, and flags: RED for restatements (8-K 4.02), delisting notices, bankruptcy and late 10-Ks; AMBER for auditor changes, cybersecurity incidents, impairments, late 10-Qs, net losses, cash burn, negative equity and shrinking revenue; GREEN for profitable growth and insider buying. `summary` says it all in a few sentences; every flag cites its filing. Replaces five separate calls (company_profile, sec_financials twice, sec_recent_events, sec_insider_trades). next_calls lead to what changed in the risk factors and the latest earnings release. Unknown, ambiguous or private companies are not charged. You are only charged when a result is returned: invalid input (400) and upstream failures (4xx/5xx) are not settled. Costs $0.03 USDC per call via x402. Paid per call with x402 inside MCP (see the server instructions).

cik.description: SEC Central Index Key, e.g. 320193. Use this, `ticker` or `company`.

company.description: Company name, e.g. "Apple" or "Coca-Cola". Use this, `ticker` or `cik`; a name matching several companies returns their tickers, free.

domain.description: The company's website, e.g. "nvidia.com". Use this, `ticker`, `cik` or `company`.

ticker.description: US stock ticker, e.g. AAPL, MSFT, BRK-B. Use this, `cik` or `company`.

via.description: Optional: the tool whose next_calls suggested this call (filled in for you).
